thread:
Alex: Heads up — ran into a tenant getting silently served v1 even though console showed their app as 'v2-ready'. Billing/latency mismatch.
Dina: repro pls?
Alex: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <tok>' \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
Alex: They didn't include X-Api-Version header (client lib omission). Runtime defaulted to v1 variant for routing reasons. Console mapping used the requested route (v2) so quotas/alerts were wrong.
Sam: Telemetry spike: routing.fallback.unmarked count ~1.2k since 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC, mostly high-seqlen tenants. Saw token billing attach to requested_route not served_variant.
Tyler: Ugh. So two problems: (1) fallback is silent, (2) billing/console uses the wrong signal for cost attribution.
Dina: Short-term mitigation ideas?
Alex: 1) have runtime return an explicit header: X-Served-Version: v1|v2, 2) emit metric routing.served_version{served,requested,tenant}, 3) console surfaces served version in per-route table and uses served_version for quota/billing mapping.
Sam: Agree. Also add an alert when served != requested for the same tenant (percent > 1% over 1h) :eyes:
Tyler: Are there any data-leak concerns with exposing X-Served-Version? We already expose model name in headers for some responses.
Dina: Security ok per prior review, but call it out in PR and docs. Also add a short retention policy for served-version metrics (30d) to avoid cost explosion.
Alex: Proposed rollout: canary header+metric (5% traffic) -> console badge to flag ambiguous requests -> switch billing/alerts to served_version -> backfill correction for last 48h for affected tenants -> deprecation UX prompting clients to set X-Api-Version.
Sam: Telemetry names please. I'll add to dashboards once decided.
Dina: Suggest metrics: "routing.requested_version", "routing.served_version", "routing.fallback_reason" (enum: header_missing, incompatible_hint, capacity_fallback), "console.version_badge_seen". Tag with request_id and tenant_id.
Sam: I'll wire those into scribe with request_id and model_name tags and add a Kibana panel. Also add a datapoint counter for billing backfill job.
Tyler: Console UX: small inline banner on per-tenant routes: "Served version differs from requested — click to view requests". And a per-tenant toggle to opt into strict-version-enforcement for 30 days (useful for testing).
Alex: Support play: if backfill shows >10% bill delta for a tenant, send templated outreach and offer adjust/credit. Otherwise just inform via console message.
Dina: Can we emit a short-term debug header too: X-Fallback-Reason: header_missing to help triage? Remove in GA maybe.
Sam: Good idea — include X-Fallback-Reason only when env=canary or header present.
deploy-bot: deploy started: routing-service v2.1.8 -> canary 5% (initiated by Tyler)
Alex: Thanks — monitor routing.served_version.* and billing.delta. If served!=requested rate doesn't drop, we roll back.
Tyler: I'll open an RFC PR with console mocks and add a small playbook for eng-sre alerts.
Dina: Looping eng-sre for alerting + billing team for backfill plan.
Alex: Filing a short incident if any tenant backfill delta >10% of their monthly bill; otherwise treat as ops task.
Sam: I'll post the initial dashboard link once metrics are ingested. Expect signal to show immediate drop in ambiguous fallbacks post-canary.
Tyler: Mock coming in ~2h. Thanks all :thumbsup:
